title: Board waiver of a 247 CMR requirement on a petition signed by the Manager of Record
subtopic: Petition for waiver of 247 CMR requirements
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 14.01(1), unless otherwise prohibited by law, the Board may waive compliance with one or more regulatory requirements set in 247 CMR if the Board finds that there is a compelling public interest which would be served by granting the waiver, that the petitioner's adherence to the waived regulatory requirements would be impractical and unduly burdensome, and that there are sufficient safeguards to protect the public health, welfare and safety without the petitioner's compliance. Under 247 CMR 14.01(2) a petition must be submitted on a form supplied by the Board and must be completed and signed by the proposed manager of record on behalf of an applicant for a pharmacy license, or by the current manager of record on behalf of a licensed pharmacy. Under 247 CMR 14.01(3) a completed petition shall list each regulatory requirement for which a waiver is requested with a brief explanation of why it should not apply to that pharmacy or pharmacy department, explain the compelling public interest and why adherence would be impractical and unduly burdensome, include a comprehensive statement of the policies and procedures of the proposed operation including safeguards to protect the public health, welfare and safety, and be accompanied by any additional information as determined by the Board. Under 247 CMR 14.01(4) the Board may require the applicant to appear personally before acting on a petition. Under 247 CMR 14.01(5), waivers granted on or before June 30, 2013 shall expire on June 30, 2018; waivers granted after June 30, 2013 expire on the fifth anniversary of the date granted; a pharmacy may submit a subsequent petition in anticipation of, or following, expiration, which must meet 247 CMR 14.01(1) through (4); and a pharmacy must comply with all regulatory requirements in 247 CMR after expiration unless the Board has granted a subsequent waiver.
exam_relevance: Tests that a waiver of a Board regulation is the Board's to grant on three findings, on a petition completed and signed by the Manager of Record for the pharmacy, and that it lapses on the fifth anniversary of the grant.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

numeric_facts.conditions: waiver granted after June 30, 2013; it expires on the fifth anniversary of the date it was granted

exceptions: The Board's authority to waive a 247 CMR requirement applies unless otherwise prohibited by law.
common_confusions: A waiver is the Board's to grant on the findings in 247 CMR 14.01(1); it is not a decision a pharmacy or a pharmacist makes for itself.
All three findings are required: a compelling public interest, adherence that would be impractical and unduly burdensome, and sufficient safeguards without compliance.
The petition is completed and signed by the current manager of record on behalf of a licensed pharmacy, or by the proposed manager of record on behalf of an applicant for a pharmacy license.
A waiver granted after June 30, 2013 expires on the fifth anniversary of its grant, after which the pharmacy must comply unless a subsequent waiver has been granted.
verification_notes: Read in full on 2026-09-16 in the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's publication of 247 CMR 14.00 on mass.gov (PDF, MA Reg. #1348, dated 9-22-17), linked from the 247 CMR 14.00 page of the Trial Court Law Libraries' 247 CMR listing.
